column1: # Best-effort-after-commit guard exemption list — GUARD-1 (#2561 for the v2 format).
# internal/core/besteffort_guard_test.go,
# server/http/handlers/besteffort_guard_test.go and
# server/grpc/services/besteffort_guard_test.go each fail the build when a
# non-test function in their package drops a call's result after a storage
# write has already committed, without routing it through
# goSafe(...)/besteffort.Run(...) (package internal/besteffort). The scanner
# itself lives in internal/besteffortguard; read its package doc for what it
# does and, more importantly, what it does NOT see.
# The bug class, found 12+ times one call site at a time by QA-1: a best-effort
# post-commit step (evict a cache, notify an admin, emit an audit event) panics,
# the panic escapes, and the caller reports FAILURE for an operation that
# actually succeeded.
# Format (3 tab-separated fields)
#   <package>:<function>#<callee>   <guard>   <reason>
# <package>  the scanned root: internal/core, server/http/handlers, or
#            server/grpc/services. Identically-named functions in different
#            packages therefore never collide.
# <function> the ENCLOSING function, as the scanner labels it ("Name", or
#            "(*Type).Name" for a method) — or "*" for a callee-level row,
#            meaning "this callee is its own panic choke point, so any caller
#            discarding its result is safe." The callee may NEVER be "*".
# <callee>   the function whose result is being dropped.
# <guard>    how this row's own safety claim is VERIFIED, not asserted:
#              callee-recovers           the callee's body defers a recover().
#              callee-recovers-via:<fn>  the callee funnels through <fn>, which
#                                        defers a recover(). Checked both ways:
#                                        <fn> must really recover, AND <fn> must
#                                        be reachable from the callee.
#              site-reviewed             a human claim no derived check covers.
#                                        The escape hatch — a row using it must
#                                        say why neither of the above applies.
# <reason>   prose, minimum 40 chars. A one-word reason is a suppression.
# What changed in v2 (#2561 coordinator review), and why the row count DROPPED
# from 12 to 3 while the guard got strictly stronger:
# 1. The key was the enclosing FUNCTION alone, which made every row a blanket
#    pardon for that whole function body. Once "(*KeyorixCore).ActivateMFA" was
#    exempt for discarding one already-self-recovering callee, a NEW
#    unprotected discard of a DIFFERENT callee added to that same function was
#    absorbed by the existing row and never flagged. The key now names the
#    callee, because that is what the claim was always about.
# 2. SEVEN of the twelve v1 rows pardoned ZERO hits — measured by running v1's
#    own scanner, not inferred. The coordinator spotted evictUserSessionCache
#    (the file's own comment admitted it was listed "for completeness of the
#    corpus"); deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict, emitAudit,
#    evictMachineIdentityCacheOrFlush, notifyBreakGlassAdmins,
#    revokeProjectDynamicSecretLeases and seedProjectEnvironment were the same
#    mistake — all six keyed as if they were enclosing functions when the claim
#    was about them as CALLEES. StaleExemptions now fails the build on a pardon
#    for nothing, because a row like that is indistinguishable from a
#    load-bearing one to anyone reading the file, and because a row that goes
#    stale by having its hit FIXED leaves the fix un-guarded: the shape can come
#    back and land straight into a pardon that is already sitting there.
# 3. The scanner saw only `_ = f(...)`. A bare `f(...)` whose result is simply
#    never assigned carries the identical panic-escape risk and was invisible.
#    Adding it found 42 further (function, callee) pairs in internal/core, every
#    one of them a dropped bool from writeAuditEventFull/writeAuditEventDiff.
#    None is a real bug — see the two callee-level rows below — but none was
#    being checked either.
# 4. Nothing proved the guard could fail. internal/besteffortguard's
#    testdata/planted/planted.go.txt is a fixture whose functions are NAMED for
#    the verdict the scanner must reach (MustFlag* / MustNotFlag*), asserted in
#    both directions, so deleting a matcher goes red there instead of
#    silently-passing in all three packages.
# 5. server/http/handlers and server/grpc/services legitimately have ZERO hits
#    (every discard in them precedes its write). Their guards therefore prove
#    nothing about hits, so they assert the scan's PRECONDITION instead —
#    FuncsWithWrite — which would collapse if the write matcher broke. "Zero
#    hits" with zero writes detected is not a clean package, it is a dead check.
# deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict (account.go) recovers its own panic, sets a
# named return (err = nil) so the discard is literally correct either way, AND
# writes EventSessionRevocationPanicked under the affected user's ID on a panic
# — bespoke audit-on-panic logic that besteffort.Run's generic recover would
# lose. Its five callers (ActivateMFA, DisableMFA, DeleteWebAuthnCredential,
# FinishWebAuthnRegistration, UpdateSCIMUser) all discard the result after a
# committed write; the protection correctly lives in the callee, which is why a
# caller-side AST walk cannot see it.
internal/core:*#deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict
column3: The callee recovers its own panic in account.go and additionally persists EventSessionRevocationPanicked for the affected user, so wrapping it again at each of its five call sites would duplicate the recover and lose that bespoke audit-on-panic record.

column1: # writeAuditEventFull / writeAuditEventDiff return "did this event durably
# persist" (added by #2406 for the few callers that need to verify it); every
# earlier caller ignores it, which is source-compatible and behaviour-unchanged.
# Both funnel into emitAudit (service.go), whose deferred recover() is the
# SINGLE choke point every c.Log*/writeAuditEvent* helper reaches — independently
# machine-proved by TestDirectLogAuditEventCallersAreSafe, which allows no other
# path to storage.LogAuditEvent. So a panic in any of these ~42 post-commit
# audit emissions is already recovered one or two hops down, and the
# callee-recovers-via guard below re-derives that reachability from the source
# on every run rather than taking this paragraph's word for it.
internal/core:*#writeAuditEventFull
column3: Thin wrapper over writeAuditEventDiff, which funnels into emitAudit; emitAudit defers a recover() and is the single choke point for every audit write (TestDirectLogAuditEventCallersAreSafe proves no other path to storage.LogAuditEvent exists), so a panic here never reaches the already-committed caller.

column1: internal/core:*#writeAuditEventDiff
column3: Funnels directly into emitAudit, whose deferred recover() is the single choke point for every audit write (TestDirectLogAuditEventCallersAreSafe proves no other path to storage.LogAuditEvent exists), so a panic here never reaches the already-committed caller.
